# How AI is Turning Flat Street Maps into Walkable Virtual Worlds

Think about the last time you tried to find a new cafe or holiday rental online, clicking through flat, static photos and wishing you could just step inside the screen to explore. While standard online maps are useful, advanced artificial intelligence is now stitching those flat images together to build fully interactive, walkable virtual worlds. 

By combining street-level photography with smart algorithms, this technology allows us to fly over neighbourhoods and walk down paths on our screens with incredible realism. Here is how this clever technology works and how you can use it to explore your world.

## The magic behind 3D mapping

Traditionally, creating a virtual 3D world required highly specialised laser scanners, expensive cameras, and hundreds of hours of manual computer programming. Today, generative AI (software that can create brand-new content, like images or 3D models, based on existing data) does the heavy lifting in seconds.

The AI takes millions of standard, flat, two-dimensional photographs of streets, buildings, and landmarks. It then uses a technique called a NeRF (neural radiance field—a technology that teaches an AI to reconstruct a complete 3D scene from a handful of flat photos). 

Think of this AI like a painter who can look at a few photos of a building and accurately paint what that building looks like from the side or from above, even though no one took a photo from those angles. The AI fills in the blanks, calculating how light, shadows, and textures should change as you move around.

## Creating realistic environments

Once the AI understands the shapes of the buildings and the layout of the streets, it layers on real-world data to make the simulation (a computer-generated model of a real environment) feel alive. 

This means you can do more than just look at a static model. These systems can simulate what a street looks like at different times of the day, how the shadows fall at sunset, or what the area looks like under different weather conditions. Some systems even overlay live traffic and weather data, letting you see how busy a street is before you step out of your door.

This level of detail makes virtual exploration incredibly practical. You can check if a restaurant has wheelchair access, see if a hotel street is well-lit at night, or find the nearest bicycle path before you even pack your bags.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life**: You can take the stress out of travel and event planning. Before booking a hotel or visiting a new suburb, use immersive map views to walk the local streets virtually, check out local parking, and see where the nearest public transport stops are.
